title: Tools
summary: A tool is a function a server advertises with a name, description and JSON Schema. The model decides when to call it with `tools/call`, and the result flows back as content, structured content or an error the model can act on.
useIf: The model must take an action or fetch data on demand, and you can describe the inputs with a schema.
avoidIf: The data is static context a host should attach itself (a resource) or a user-picked workflow (a prompt).

explain.md: A tool definition has `name`, `title`, `description`, `icons`, `inputSchema`, an optional `outputSchema` and `annotations` [[r37]]. Names SHOULD be 1 to 128 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, hyphen and dot, and unique per server. A client or proxy that merges servers SHOULD prefix names with a server identifier to avoid collisions [[r6]].

**Discovery** is `tools/list`. In 2026-07-28 the result carries `ttlMs` and `cacheScope`, servers SHOULD return a deterministic order, and the list MUST NOT vary per connection, though it MAY vary by the authorization on the request. A change is announced with `notifications/tools/list_changed` on a `subscriptions/listen` stream. In 2025-11-25 it arrived on a server-to-client stream inside the session.

**Invocation** is `tools/call` with `name` and `arguments`. The result holds `content` blocks (text, image, audio, `resource_link` or an embedded resource), optional `structuredContent` and `isError`. There are two error kinds. Protocol errors (unknown tool, malformed request) are JSON-RPC errors. Execution errors, including input validation failures, use `isError: true` so the model can read the message and retry (a change made in 2025-11-25 [[r31]]) [[r6]].

explain.title: From catalog to result
explain.alt: The host lists tools from the server, gives definitions to the model, the model requests a call, the host calls the server and returns the result to the model.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Host
  participant S as Server
  participant M as Model
  H->>S: tools/list
  S-->>H: definitions, ttlMs
  H->>M: prompt and definitions
  M-->>H: call get_order
  H->>S: tools/call
  S-->>H: content, isError
  H->>M: result

explain.title: A tools/call request in 2026-07-28 (shortened)
explain.caption: Each request carries version and capabilities in `_meta`. A 2025-11-25 request instead relied on the session set up by `initialize`.

explain.title: Keep a human in the loop
explain.md: The spec says there SHOULD be a human able to deny tool invocations, with clear indicators when tools run. Clients MUST treat annotations as untrusted unless the server is trusted, and servers MUST validate inputs, enforce access control, rate limit and sanitize outputs.

whereToUse: Actions with side effects: create a ticket, send a message, deploy a build
On-demand lookups the model cannot predict: search, query, fetch by id
Computation the model should not do itself: calculations, code execution in a sandbox
Workflow tools that bundle several API calls into one outcome

use: The model should choose when and with what arguments
The input fits a JSON Schema
The result is small enough to put in context, or can be a link
avoid: The content is a fixed document the host should attach (resource)
A user should pick a canned workflow (prompt)
The call needs a human decision on every use and no approval path exists
flips: Result payloads are large: return a summary plus a `resource_link`
Many similar tools pile up: consolidate into workflow tools or use tool search

pitfalls.symptom: The wrong server's tool runs when two servers both expose `search`
pitfalls.cause: Names are unique per server only and the aggregator did not prefix them
pitfalls.fix: Prefix names with a server identifier and keep descriptions specific

pitfalls.symptom: The agent loops on a bad date argument
pitfalls.cause: Validation failed as a JSON-RPC protocol error, which clients may not feed back to the model
pitfalls.fix: Return `isError: true` with an actionable message such as the expected format

pitfalls.symptom: Latency and token cost jump after adding a report tool
pitfalls.cause: A large payload is pushed through the context window on every call
pitfalls.fix: Return a summary plus a `resource_link`, or paginate with sensible defaults

scenarios.title: A refund tool with side effects
scenarios.situation: An agent may issue customer refunds through a server owned by the payments team. A mistaken call moves real money. Volume is a few hundred calls a day.
constraints: Server is third-party to the host
unknowns: Is there an approval policy by amount?
Does the payments API support idempotency keys?
Who is the caller identity downstream?
scenarios.question: How do you expose and guard it?

options.name: A tool with host approval and an idempotency key argument
options.why: Keeps the model in charge of choosing the call while a human confirms the money movement, and the key prevents double refunds on retry.
options.tradeoff: Approval prompts add friction and need a reviewer.

options.name: A prompt the user triggers manually
options.tradeoff: The agent cannot act on its own, which loses the point of automation.

options.name: Auto-approve because the tool is marked destructiveHint false
options.why: Annotations are hints and MUST be treated as untrusted unless the server is trusted.
options.tradeoff: Trusting hints is acceptable only for servers you operate and review.

flips.if: Refunds below a small amount may be automated
flips.then: Approve by policy in the host and require a human above a threshold.
Move to policy-based approvals plus after-the-fact review.

scenarios.takeaway: Side effects need approval and idempotency, not trust in hints.

scenarios.title: A report that returns 80,000 tokens
scenarios.situation: A `get_report` tool returns the full text of a quarterly report. The assistant usually needs only a few figures. Context is limited and cost matters.
constraints: Most turns need a small part
unknowns: Can the report be summarised or sliced server side?
Does the host support resource links?
scenarios.question: What should the tool return?

options.name: A short summary plus a `resource_link` to the full report
options.why: The model sees what it needs and the host can read the full resource only when required.
options.tradeoff: Needs a server-side summary and a client that handles resource links.

options.name: Paginated sections with a cursor argument
options.why: Bounds each result and lets the model ask for more.
options.tradeoff: Several round trips for a full read.

options.name: The whole report as text content
options.why: Every call pays the full token cost and crowds out the conversation.
options.tradeoff: Fine only when payloads are small.

flips.if: The task is to summarise the whole report
flips.then: Returning the whole text once is justified.

flips.if: The host cannot render or follow resource links
flips.then: Use pagination or a search tool that returns relevant slices.

scenarios.takeaway: Bound result size and let large data travel by reference.

quiz.q: An agent keeps retrying a booking with a bad date format. The server answers every time with JSON-RPC error -32602. What is the best fix?
options: Return a tool result with `isError: true` and a message naming the expected format
Switch the tool to a resource
quiz.explain: Input validation failures are tool execution errors, which clients SHOULD show to the model so it can self-correct. Protocol errors are less likely to lead to recovery. More retries, a resource or no schema do not give the model the information it lacks.

quiz.q: Which content types can a tool result carry?
quiz.explain: Tool results may hold text, image, audio, resource links and embedded resources, plus optional structured content. A raw cursor object is not a content type.

flashcards.front: What two error kinds exist for tool calls?
flashcards.back: Protocol errors (JSON-RPC, such as unknown tool) and tool execution errors (`isError: true`), which the model can read and fix.

flashcards.front: Who controls tools, and what should still apply?
flashcards.back: The model decides when to call them. A human SHOULD be able to deny invocations, and annotations are untrusted unless the server is trusted.
Results carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope`, servers SHOULD use a deterministic order, and change notifications come over `subscriptions/listen`.
